title: Online Proctoring Compliance
tagline: Year 4 — Following proctoring instructions: identity checks, camera and microphone, environment, devices and what to do when something goes wrong

introduction.overview: Many online assessments are proctored: the test provider checks identity, may watch through the camera and screen, and records the session. The rules differ between employers and providers, so the only reliable guide is the official instructions. In general, compliance means: verify your identity as instructed, set up a quiet and tidy space, keep to the permitted devices and materials, stay in the camera frame if required, do not share or capture questions, and report technical problems through the official channel. Honesty and compliance protect you; violations can disqualify you. The rules and figures used in examples are hypothetical teaching rules, not the policy of any real company or platform.
introduction.placementRelevance: A technical or rule violation can end an attempt regardless of the score.
introduction.realWorldContext: Following procedure in a regulated process is a professional expectation.

learningObjectives: Behave in line with camera and screen rules

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: When in doubt, follow the official instructions or ask the designated support channel before the test starts.

coreDefinitions: Proctoring: supervision of a test, live or recorded.
Identity verification: showing that you are the candidate.
Permitted materials: items the instructions allow.
Support channel: the official way to report problems.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Proctoring is about trust; clear compliance protects your result.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Before: read the rules, prepare ID and space. During: stay within rules. After a problem: stop and use the support channel.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: During
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Stay in frame, no other tools

mainNarrative: The day before: read the instructions, charge the device, check the network, prepare identity documents, and choose a quiet room.
On the day: log in early, complete identity checks as instructed, clear the desk of unauthorised items, and keep your face in the frame if the instructions require it.
If the connection drops: do not try to improvise. Reconnect if possible and report through the official support channel immediately, noting the time and the problem.
Do not photograph, copy or share questions: it is a violation and unfair to others.
If an instruction is unclear, ask the support channel before the test starts.
